batch_strategy: Scaffold-specific late-tail repair with paired condition ladders and loading contrasts

choices.reason: High-width, high-CW m146 point at 10/1 and higher loading extends the measured m146 response toward the late regime seen in 9e3ce3497298084abd83; it can teach both endpoint calibration and loading sensitivity.
The broad predicted m146 point at 5/1 and low loading fills the transition between the ordinary 1/1 observation b6229f0445560a4a54ed and the late 10/1 observation 9e3ce3497298084abd83.

This m82 10/1 low-loading point forms a direct loading contrast with the measured 10/1 row 6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216; its wide predicted interval tests whether the tail is already activated at lower amount.
The m82 10/1 higher-volume point completes a local loading ladder around 6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216 and can distinguish smooth amount dependence from a threshold-like late regime.

A broad m72 10/1, 150-ul DCM point extends the measured 10/1 low-volume behavior in 7383949c431e18f39597; the label is useful for learning whether V2 expands with loading before V1 shifts substantially.
This m72 5/1 PE point contrasts with the measured 5/1 higher-volume point 1f70add69a6dbecca3b4 and with the stronger 10/1 tail 542f504077b58e444bc2, testing condition and loading interaction.

The m96 50/1 candidate has very broad predicted endpoint widths and high CW distance in an underrepresented sulfur-containing scaffold, making its label a useful transfer test for late-tail calibration.
This high-width m94 20/1 point probes whether the ordinary m94 observations such as 7bd353fc307c5af1997e and 20d4b1612cbdd88b6755 transition into a broad late interval at stronger eluent.
The m78 50/1, 150-ul point extends the measured m78 strong-condition tails 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760 and 61771d230b285babe4b6 to a new loading level, directly testing endpoint-asymmetric loading effects.

This m205 candidate is a high-CW, extremely broad predicted late point despite the low-regime measured anchor 0483db40cbad8db07032; it can reveal whether this scaffold has a sharp condition-triggered retention transition.
The broad m207 10/1 point complements the measured strong-condition behavior in a19f98569910dc7fd6c4 and 4e5ead91320bd24d485e, testing whether the late tail changes with loading amount.
This high-width m135 point creates a condition/loading contrast with measured m135 rows 716d04ed1943f0708912 and 75232f4ee5de52a0499e, where late behavior is already apparent.

The m99 10/1 high-loading candidate has a very broad predicted interval and high CW distance; together with the low-regime measured anchor 83326d8b972b1f3325e4 it tests transfer of tail behavior into a lightly sampled condition region.
This m114 intermediate-strength point fills the gap between the measured 10/1 behavior cde49c2f3cf630c3a2a2 and the strong 50/1 tails 44fcf641ccfa3b10a97c and 0cf0d36290765378ae8d.
The m206 1/1, 50-ul point fills the condition ladder between measured 0/1 behavior b0f83f107759037eea65 and 2/1 behavior 7c0c324643799c918828, helping locate onset of the observed late tail.
This m206 1/1, 150-ul point pairs with the lower-loading m206 candidate and measured 2/1 and 5/1 tail points 13bfaf03c35b4cff3bd5, a6145bb0c9947f9515df, and 614873124b33029a924c.
The m206 0/1, 150-ul point extends the measured 0/1 loading behavior represented by b0f83f107759037eea65 and 18d688363c7fa3da0609, separating amount effects from solvent-strength effects.
This m120 2/1, 150-ul point bridges the measured 2/1 low-volume point 4ee22742c686bdbb1cb9 and the much later 5/1 observations 71abc36775b6cce56da7 and 20913a7c2077b80b7351.
The m125 1/1, 50-ul point at a new loading-solvent volume is a controlled contrast to measured 00043aebb2540e369a7b and tests whether the scaffold's broad interval depends on loading preparation.

This m125 0/1, 100-ul point provides a low-strength loading-solvent anchor next to measured low-regime m125 behavior e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2, useful for separating baseline calibration from the later tail.
The m125 1/1, 100-ul point completes a local amount and condition comparison with the other selected m125 rows and measured 4c32851430464f0ed684.

This m55 30/1 point is an intermediate condition anchor between the measured 10/1 point a62a679c00aad3b9b8e5 and the accurate 40/1 point c32ed74eba9d7dfc4860, directly testing curve smoothness and nonlinearity.
The m159 1/1, 100-ul point fills the gap between measured low-condition behavior 7945dfcb6be718f22113 and the much later 20/1 and 50/1 observations a738b1f204da6fcfd385 and a17bcdddcf0799baeee2.

This m204 2/1, 50-ul point tests the onset of the strong retention shift between measured low-condition behavior a3a9c58c8aa6145907a6 and the higher-loading observations 6a39aff909ea35989c74 and b7b1a1bb666c8cc99bad.
The m160 1/1, 150-ul candidate interpolates between measured 1/1 behavior fbf7711e24f45bf06d4f, 2/1 behavior 36d971e3231c54486d05, and the severe 5/1 tails ad833f34f6b91872362d.

This molecule-condition point probes a strong 50/1 transition in m157 after the measured 5/1 high-loading anchor ef66ddd22d87be908947, adding a halogenated scaffold response curve with broad model uncertainty.
The m208 20/1, 50-ul point links measured lower-condition behavior e71bdbb1d06ba82dc4cc with the strong tails 0b8c6c59ae5e24b420e5 and 95d1d257dfea69f178f8, while testing loading dependence.
This m197 50/1 low-loading phenolic point tests whether the late response seen at 0/1 in ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3 and at 20/1 in 8de30a7f5764c20b232e persists at stronger eluent.
The m40 50/1, 150-ul point extends the measured strong-condition m40 tail 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49 to a different loading amount, providing direct information on tail position and width.

Molecule-novel m145 supplies an ordinary intermediate-condition anchor with moderate model uncertainty and limited similarity, protecting overall Row-distribution coverage while the batch repairs tails.

This high-CW m21 intermediate-condition point adds a chemically distinct aromatic ether example and tests whether its broad predicted interval transfers from the ordinary low-condition neighborhood represented by bda6ee6b2ab7b1212866.
The broad m107 5/1 point samples a stronger condition in a less represented oxygen-rich scaffold, complementing ordinary anchors and testing tail transfer across chemical neighborhoods.

hypotheses.content: Condition-response curves are scaffold-specific and can be nonlinear; stronger eluent often expands V2 much more than V1 in tail-prone scaffolds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor needs scaffold-specific solvent-strength response structure and endpoint-specific corrections rather than a single global shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected intermediate condition points locate a smooth transition, or a threshold at which V2 expands abruptly?

hypotheses.content: Loading effects are molecule- and endpoint-specific, with V2 often more sensitive than V1 in broad regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched amount and loading-solvent contrasts can teach whether the model should represent position, width, or regime activation separately for V1 and V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the apparent loading responses smooth within a scaffold, or do they activate only after retention becomes strong?

hypotheses.content: Large remaining failures are concentrated in conditional late tails across fused, phenolic, basic, and heteroaromatic neighborhoods, with possible transfer to nearby scaffolds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These high-absolute-error regions can dominate joint V1/V2 loss, and targeted labels may improve calibration across chemically related rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do high-width predictions in additional scaffolds reproduce the measured late tails, or are the failures family-specific?

hypotheses.content: Coverage of ordinary, molecule-novel, and intermediate-width rows is needed alongside tail repair to improve generalization across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A batch dominated only by extreme tails could overfit failure neighborhoods; ordinary and molecule-novel anchors help preserve calibration and chemical coverage elsewhere.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After adding these anchors, which chemical and condition regions still have broad predictions without nearby labels?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthen the split between ordinary anchors and conditional late tails. The m69 baseline 53c0ebdf849859e3432e was nearly accurate, while m150 be17b1e2add7cad714b5 was accurate for V1 but overpredicted V2 modestly. In contrast, m197 ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3, m40 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49, m216 e47aebe2660b9e1528de and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321, m206 b7cf293311f83700cd9a, and m159 a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 showed substantial late-regime errors. The accurate m55 contrasts a62a679c00aad3b9b8e5 and c32ed74eba9d7dfc4860 suggest that some response curves are locally learnable, so this batch emphasizes intermediate condition anchors and loading ladders around tail-prone scaffolds rather than applying a universal correction.
batch_rationale: The batch combines three complementary learning targets. First, high-width and high-CW rows across m146, m82, m72, m96, m94, m78, m205, m207, m135, m99, m197, m40, and m107 repair chemically distinct late-tail regions implicated by measured failures. Second, paired rows for m206, m125, m120, m159, m204, m160, m208, and m55 create local condition or amount-response experiments, including intermediate points between accurate and extreme observations. Third, the molecule-novel m145 anchor and chemically distinct intermediate points preserve ordinary Row-distribution coverage. This structure should help the retrained model learn when V2 widens, when V1 shifts with it, and when broad model predictions are simply conservative in otherwise ordinary regimes.
